reply.recognition: Recognized as the UCI Beijing PM2.5 dataset (UCI 381), including its listed 2015 introduction paper. This recognition does not supply a novelty claim or an unverified result from that paper.
reply.summary: Goal: propose a testable question about pollution episodes or response decisions beyond next-hour prediction. The supplied evidence describes one hourly Beijing monitoring series (2010-2014), 2,067 missing PM2.5 values, meteorology from the airport, and no direct emissions or intervention measures. Candidate tests therefore concern observed episode dynamics and remain observational.

candidates.title: Do wind-direction transitions add information about episode clearance?
candidates.question: Among high-PM2.5 episodes, does a change in recorded wind direction predict sustained clearance within six hours beyond concentration history, season/hour, and recorded Iws?
candidates.new_claim: Input delta: the input lists hourly concentration and wind variables but does not pose episode clearance as an outcome or test whether direction transitions add information after matching on prior concentration and recorded wind-speed values. This is a candidate question, not a world-literature novelty claim.
candidates.domain_value: Could help air-quality teams identify when an episode may clear and avoid relying on a concentration-only persistence rule. The result would support an observational alert feature, not a causal intervention or transport attribution.
assumptions: For an operational pilot, define episode entry as PM2.5 >=150 ug/m^3 after a preceding observed value below 150; define clearance as PM2.5 <75 ug/m^3 for three consecutive observed hours, reached within six hours of the index hour. These thresholds are proposed design choices, not supplied standards.
A change in cbwd is a coarse air-mass/ventilation proxy; cbwd and Iws do not measure source location or emissions, and Iws is documented as cumulated wind speed.
Missing PM2.5 hours interrupt episode and clearance classification; treating them as clearance would bias the result.

variables_and_units.episode_entry: PM2.5 >=150 ug/m^3 following an observed value below 150
variables_and_units.clearance: PM2.5 <75 ug/m^3 for 3 consecutive observed hourly readings within 6 h
variables_and_units.recorded_wind: Iws, documented m/s; use as a recorded covariate, not an instantaneous wind measurement
variables_and_units.matching_covariates: index PM2.5 (ug/m^3), recent PM2.5 history (ug/m^3), month and hour, Iws

candidates.testable_prediction: In held-out contiguous time blocks, episodes with a direction transition at the index hour will have a higher six-hour sustained-clearance rate than comparable episodes without a transition, after matching or adjustment for index and recent PM2.5, month/hour, and recorded Iws. Freeze this positive incremental prediction before computation.
candidates.alternative: Direction transitions add no clearance information once recent PM2.5, season/hour, and recorded Iws are accounted for; apparent gains arise from temporal clustering, missing readings, or calendar composition.
candidates.discriminating_test: Use episode as the analysis unit, compare a prespecified baseline using prior PM2.5 history, month/hour, and Iws with the same model plus the direction-transition indicator, and evaluate held-out contiguous blocks or years. Report the event count, missingness exclusions, clearance-rate difference, and uncertainty. Do not split adjacent hours from the same episode across train and test.
candidates.feasible_with_current_data: Yes, as a single-series observational feasibility test if enough complete episodes exist. Five years and one station limit independent replication; missing PM2.5 and autocorrelation must be handled explicitly.
candidates.required_new_data: For a causal transport or response claim: simultaneous upwind/downwind PM2.5 and wind vectors, source/emissions information, and intervention timing. These are not needed for the narrower historical association test.
candidates.failure_condition: The direction-transition addition has no positive held-out clearance-rate increment over the matched baseline, or its sign is unstable across held-out blocks; also fail feasibility if too few complete episodes remain for a meaningful estimate.
candidates.nearest_prior_query: Search for studies testing wind-direction changes as incremental predictors of urban PM2.5 episode termination or clearance, conditional on concentration history and wind speed; compare this proposed episode-level held-out contrast with existing work.

candidates.title: Does rain onset change short-term episode decay?
candidates.question: When the recorded cumulative-rain-hours field first increases during a high-PM2.5 episode, is the subsequent six-hour PM2.5 change more negative than in comparable no-increase windows?
candidates.new_claim: Input delta: the input supplies Ir and PM2.5 but does not define rain onset from changes in Ir or compare post-onset episode decay against matched dry windows. This tests an observed contrast, not a causal rain effect.
candidates.domain_value: Could clarify whether the available precipitation proxy is useful for episode monitoring and alert updates.
assumptions: Use a positive one-hour change in Ir, documented as cumulated hours of rain, only as a rain-hour proxy; it is not rainfall amount or intensity.
Compare windows with similar starting PM2.5, recent trend, month/hour, cbwd, and Iws; residual weather and emissions confounding remain.

variables_and_units.outcome: PM2.5 at t+6 minus PM2.5 at t, ug/m^3
variables_and_units.matching: starting PM2.5 and recent trend in ug/m^3; month/hour; cbwd; Iws in documented m/s

candidates.testable_prediction: Matched windows with a positive Ir increment have a more negative median six-hour PM2.5 change than windows without an increment.
candidates.alternative: The contrast is absent after matching or reflects co-occurring wind/calendar changes rather than precipitation scavenging.
candidates.discriminating_test: Identify positive Ir increments during qualifying episodes and match to complete dry windows on starting concentration, recent slope, season/hour, cbwd, and Iws; compare six-hour changes using episode-level held-out blocks.
candidates.feasible_with_current_data: Exploratory test is feasible if Ir increments and complete PM2.5 windows are sufficiently frequent; availability and interpretation of increments must be checked.
candidates.required_new_data: Rainfall amount/intensity and an independent precipitation gauge for mechanism interpretation; emissions or intervention data for causal attribution.
candidates.failure_condition: No more negative held-out six-hour change after matching, an unstable sign across blocks, or too few eligible rain-onset windows.
candidates.nearest_prior_query: Search for observational and intervention studies comparing PM2.5 episode decay after rainfall onset with matched dry periods, especially work using cumulative rain-hour proxies.

candidates.title: Does humid stagnation amplify observed episode persistence?
candidates.question: During high-PM2.5 episodes, is persistence greater when small dewpoint depression coincides with low recorded Iws than expected from the separate associations of these conditions?
candidates.new_claim: Input delta: the input contains TEMP, DEWP, Iws, and PM2.5 but does not pose their joint condition as a test of episode persistence. The proposed interaction is a hypothesis; the dataset cannot distinguish true dry-aerosol persistence from humidity-related monitor response.
candidates.domain_value: Could reveal whether meteorological context changes the reliability of a persistence-based episode alert and motivate a targeted measurement study.
assumptions: TEMP-DEWP in degrees C is a dewpoint-depression proxy, not a direct relative-humidity measure.
Low Iws is only a proxy based on the recorded field and its cumulative definition limits a stagnation interpretation.
An observed PM2.5 interaction cannot establish hygroscopic growth or emissions mechanisms.

variables_and_units.outcome: persistence of PM2.5 >=150 ug/m^3 over subsequent observed hours

candidates.testable_prediction: The joint small-dewpoint-depression/low-Iws condition is associated with longer held-out high-PM2.5 episode persistence than predicted by additive dewpoint-depression and Iws terms.
candidates.alternative: No positive interaction remains after season, hour, prior concentration, and episode history are controlled; any interaction may be measurement response rather than increased dry-particle loading.
candidates.discriminating_test: Fit prespecified additive and interaction contrasts for episode persistence, evaluate on contiguous held-out blocks, and report episode counts and missingness. A separate co-located dry-reference PM measurement would distinguish ambient persistence from humidity-sensitive measurement response.
candidates.feasible_with_current_data: The observational interaction is testable if there are enough episodes spanning both conditions, but mechanism attribution is not feasible with current measurements.
candidates.required_new_data: Co-located humidity, wind speed/direction vectors, and dry-reference PM2.5; emissions data would help interpret sources.
candidates.failure_condition: No positive held-out interaction or insufficient episode overlap across joint meteorological conditions.
candidates.nearest_prior_query: Search for studies separating humidity-related optical or mass-monitor response from true PM2.5 episode persistence under stagnant conditions.

task.deliverable: Critique and sharpen I1 into one preregisterable episode-level contrast using only supplied fields. Return the event and missing-data rules, a comparison that distinguishes incremental direction information from a concentration-history/calendar/wind baseline, and a concise assessment of identifiability and novelty limits.
acceptance: Keep the frozen positive prediction and explicit alternative visible; do not retrofit thresholds or direction categories after seeing outcomes.
Specify episode as the analysis unit and keep adjacent hours or episodes in contiguous held-out blocks; report whether missing values or event counts make the contrast infeasible.
Do not claim causal transport, intervention effects, or world-literature novelty from this series; distinguish observed support from a proposed mechanism.

If computation is requested, make one compact broker request that checks the actual premise and states the outputs needed to assess it; if literature is searched, state how a finding would change the candidate.
task.proposed_computation: If feasible, compare held-out six-hour sustained-clearance rates for episodes with versus without an index-hour cbwd transition, matched or adjusted on index/recent PM2.5, month/hour, and recorded Iws; keep episode blocks intact and return event counts, exclusions, contrast, and uncertainty. This is a requested analysis description, not a result.
task.proposed_search: Search Crossref for work on wind-direction transitions and PM2.5 pollution episode clearance beyond concentration persistence and wind speed; report only supported title/metadata-level comparison and whether it changes the novelty framing.
